info.title: lucy API
info.description: One typed API behind every lucy surface: JSON-RPC 2.0, one request per POST to /rpc/v1, over the daemon's unix socket (and HTTPS for remote surfaces, from m1). See ADR D10.

methods.name: rpc.discover
methods.summary: The API's OpenRPC document: every method, its params, result and errors.

methods.name: hello
methods.summary: Negotiate the API version and learn the caller's identity, scopes and the methods it may call.

params.name: client
params.description: The calling surface, for example lucy-cli.

params.name: client_version
params.description: The calling surface's version.

params.name: api_versions
params.description: API major versions the client speaks.

api_version.description: The API version chosen: the highest both sides speak.

caller.description: Who the daemon thinks is calling.

actor.description: The caller's name in the event log.

device.description: local for the socket; a paired device's id remotely.

pid.description: The peer's process id, when the OS reports it.

scopes.description: The scopes granted to this caller.

transport.description: unix, or https once remote control lands.

uid.description: The peer's user id on the unix socket.

methods.description: The methods this caller's scopes allow.

methods.name: health
methods.summary: Liveness: the daemon is up and its event store answers.

status.description: ok when the daemon and its event store answer.

methods.name: status.get
methods.summary: The daemon's version, uptime and event log head.

event_head.description: Sequence number of the last event in the log; 0 when empty.

refused_connections.description: Socket connections refused since start (another user, or no peer credentials).

supervisors.description: Each org that opts into a model supervisor: its tokens today against its daily budget.

armed.description: Whether the org's models are asked: the daemon was started with --supervise and the org names them. Its rules apply either way.

daily_tokens.description: The org's daily budget; once spent, questions go straight to the owner.

day.description: The UTC day the tokens are counted in, YYYY-MM-DD.

route.description: The org's gateway route its model calls go through.

tokens.description: Tokens the supervisor spent for the org on that day, input and output.

methods.name: events.list
methods.summary: Events from the log after a sequence number, oldest first.

params.name: after_seq
params.description: Return events with a sequence number greater than this; 0 starts at the beginning.

params.name: limit
params.description: At most this many events; 0 means 100.

payload.description: The typed payload as stored; events never carry secrets.

stream.description: The stream the event belongs to.

head.description: The log's head when the page was read.

more.description: Whether events after this page existed when it was read.

next.description: Pass as after_seq to read the next page.

methods.name: daemon.shutdown
methods.summary: Stop the daemon gracefully after answering.

stopping.description: True: the daemon stops after this response.

methods.name: policy.evaluate
methods.summary: Ask the policy engine to decide an action; the decision is recorded before it is returned.

params.name: kind
params.description: The action: read, write, merge, delete, force_push, branch_delete, history_rewrite, credential_use, exec, fetch or container.

params.name: org
params.description: The org the target belongs to.

params.name: project
params.description: The project (repository), when the action has one.

params.name: resource
params.description: What the action is on: a PR (pr/12), an absolute path, a branch or a credential name.

params.name: inputs
params.description: What the request is based on, each with its source. The caller's own request is added as an owner input.

ref.description: A reference to the input: an event, URL or comment id. Never the text itself.

source.description: owner, config, daemon, task, agent, tool_output, repo_content, issue, pr_body, pr_comment, web or email.

action_sha256.description: The digest of the action (actor, kind, target) an approval must name.

approvals_used.description: The approval decisions a clearance rested on, in the order the rules used them (a fixed-list owner approval before a relayed client confirmation); empty when denied or holding.

facts_sha256.description: The digest of the facts the approver saw (a merge's head SHA, base ref and base SHA; a delete's resolved path; a credential's scope; the default branch for force-push, branch delete and history rewrite) an approval must also name; an approval for the same action under other facts is denied.

id.description: The decision's position in the policy stream; pass as after to page.

outcome.description: cleared, denied or holding (waiting on the owner).

reason.description: Why, in one line. {owner} stands for the owner; render it with the configured display title.

resource.description: The target resource. A shell command, URL or search (exec, fetch) is redacted and capped, followed by sha256:<hex> of the original.

ruleset_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of that rule set.

ruleset_version.description: The version of the rule set that decided.

seq.description: The decision event's position in the whole log.

tainted.description: Whether any input came from an untrusted source.

methods.name: policy.decisions
methods.summary: Recorded policy decisions, oldest first.

params.name: after
params.description: Return decisions with an id greater than this; 0 starts at the beginning.

params.name: limit
params.description: At most this many decisions; 0 means 100.

action_sha256.description: The digest of the action (actor, kind, target) an approval must name.

approvals_used.description: The approval decisions a clearance rested on, in the order the rules used them (a fixed-list owner approval before a relayed client confirmation); empty when denied or holding.

facts_sha256.description: The digest of the facts the approver saw (a merge's head SHA, base ref and base SHA; a delete's resolved path; a credential's scope; the default branch for force-push, branch delete and history rewrite) an approval must also name; an approval for the same action under other facts is denied.

id.description: The decision's position in the policy stream; pass as after to page.

outcome.description: cleared, denied or holding (waiting on the owner).

reason.description: Why, in one line. {owner} stands for the owner; render it with the configured display title.

resource.description: The target resource. A shell command, URL or search (exec, fetch) is redacted and capped, followed by sha256:<hex> of the original.

ruleset_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of that rule set.

ruleset_version.description: The version of the rule set that decided.

seq.description: The decision event's position in the whole log.

tainted.description: Whether any input came from an untrusted source.

more.description: Whether decisions after this page existed when it was read.

next.description: Pass as after to read the next page.

methods.name: resources.list
methods.summary: The config resources the daemon loaded and their status, as conditions.

params.name: offset
params.description: Skip this many resources; 0 starts at the beginning.

params.name: limit
params.description: At most this many resources; 0 means 100.

last_reload.description: The last config reload's outcome, when it was not applied; absent when the daemon runs on the config it last loaded.

at.description: When the reload ran, RFC 3339 UTC.

outcome.description: failed: the config directory could not be read, so the last good config stays whole; refused: some resources were refused, so the last good config stays but for the tightening.

reason.description: Why the directory could not be read, when the reload failed.

refused.description: How many resources were refused, when the reload was refused.

more.description: Whether resources after this page existed when it was read.

next.description: Pass as offset to read the next page.

refused.description: Files and documents the latest load refused that name no resource: a parse error, a missing or invalid kind, name or namespace, or a duplicate. On the first page (offset 0) only; empty on the others.

last_transition_time.description: When the status last changed, RFC 3339 UTC.

message.description: What a person needs to know.

reason.description: A machine-readable reason, for example SchemaViolation.
Why it was refused, the Valid condition's reason, for example MissingNamespace.

source.description: The file it came from, relative to the config directory, and the document's position in it.

refused_truncated.description: Refusals the latest load left out of refused, beyond the 32 it records.

resources.description: The resources and their current status.

last_transition_time.description: When the status last changed, RFC 3339 UTC.

message.description: What a person needs to know.

reason.description: A machine-readable reason, for example SchemaViolation.

name.description: The resource's name, unique per namespace and kind.

namespace.description: The airspace (org) the resource belongs to.

source.description: The file it came from, relative to the config directory, and the document's position in it.

spec_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical spec, defaults applied; empty when the resource was refused.

methods.name: audit.verify
methods.summary: Verify the audit hash chain against the event log.

broken_at_seq.description: The event whose entry failed, when broken.

entries.description: Entries verified; when broken, the entries before the break.

head.description: The last entry's hash, when verified.

reason.description: Why the chain is broken, when it is.

verified.description: True when every entry hashes correctly, links to the one before it and matches its event.

methods.name: runner.queued
methods.summary: How many runs wait for a runner placed at placement, of the runner's org when it names one. A runner polls this and leases only when it is not zero, so an idle runner adds nothing to the log. A runner placed in a container is not counted the runs of an org whose container is being restarted or stopped.

params.name: placement
params.description: The asking runner's placement: host (this machine; the default) or container (an org's container).

params.name: org
params.description: The asking runner's org: when set, only that org's runs are counted.

methods.name: runner.lease
methods.summary: Lease the oldest queued run of the runner's org under a new fencing token. A runner names its org, or is refused with runner_org. On the host that org must be the host org (the first host lease sets it; runner.host_org changes it), or the lease is refused with host_org. A runner placed in a container is leased only with a placement proof the daemon accepts, or is refused with placement_proof, and while its org's container is being restarted or stopped it is refused with sandbox_busy and leases again later.

params.name: runner
params.description: The runner's id: 1-63 of a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' and '-', starting with a letter or digit.

params.name: placement
params.description: host (this machine; the default) or container (an org's container).

params.name: org
params.description: The one org whose runs the runner leases. Required: a lease without one is refused with runner_org. On the host it must be the host org, or the lease is refused with host_org.

params.name: placement_proof
params.description: A runner placed in a container: the Sandbox provider's proof of that placement. A placement a runner declares is never trusted; until berth can issue a proof (berth#216) no daemon accepts one, and every container lease is refused with placement_proof.

params.name: ttl_seconds
params.description: The lease's life; 0 means 60, and values below 5 mean 5.

leased.description: False when no run was queued; run is then empty.

branch.description: With worktree: the branch the run works on.

capability.description: The run's capability token for its org's gateway: valid only while this lease is held, for the org's gateway routes, until it expires (five minutes, renewed by each heartbeat) or is revoked. lucy keeps only its digest; give it to nothing but the run's own gateway calls.

expires_at.description: When the lease expires unless renewed, UTC.

fence.description: The fencing token: name it on every heartbeat and finish. Fences only grow; an old one is refused.

flight.description: The flight (task) the run is for.

generation.description: The flight's Pilot generation: 1, then +1 for each replacement.

goal.description: What the run is for. Data for the work, never instructions to lucy.

org.description: The org (airspace) the run belongs to.

run.description: The run's id; a Pilot run is <flight>#<generation>.

worktree.description: When the run is placed on the host and its project names a repository: the absolute path, on the daemon's host, of the run's slot of lucy's worktree pool, which the daemon prepares (reset to the base and checked out on branch) after the lease. The run works there once it is ready.

worktree_deadline.description: With worktree: when the daemon stops preparing it at the latest, UTC.

worktree_error.description: When the run's project names a repository but no slot could be leased for it: why (worktree_state is failed). The runner then fails the run without starting it.

worktree_state.description: With worktree, or worktree_error: preparing, or failed. Hold a preparing lease, heartbeating as usual, without starting the work; start it once a heartbeat reports ready, and finish the run as failed if one reports failed or the preparation is still not done a while past worktree_deadline.

methods.name: runner.heartbeat
methods.summary: Renew a lease and record the run's newly streamed events, in one transaction.

params.name: runner
params.description: The runner holding the lease.

params.name: run
params.description: The leased run.

params.name: fence
params.description: The lease's fencing token.

params.name: ttl_seconds
params.description: The renewed life; 0 means 60, and values below 5 mean 5.

params.name: events
params.description: The run's new events, numbered from 1 without gaps; a resent event is skipped.

hook.description: The harness lifecycle hook that fired: required on a hook event, refused on any other. SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Notification, Stop, SubagentStop, PreCompact or SessionEnd.

kind.description: output, activity, asking, hook or usage.

question.description: The question's id: required on an asking event and the same on every repeat of the question, refused on any other. An asking event for an answered question is recorded as activity.

seq.description: The event's number in its run, from 1.

text.description: The event's text: a line of output, a summary, or the question. Untrusted.

tokens.description: A usage event's token use, one step of the work: required on a usage event, refused on any other.

cache_read.description: Input tokens read from the prompt cache.

cache_write.description: Input tokens written to the prompt cache.

params.name: acked
params.description: The id of the question whose answer, from an earlier heartbeat's result, the runner gave its work. Until it is acknowledged the answer comes again in every result. An id the owner did not answer under this lease is ignored.

accepted.description: The highest event number recorded for the run.

answer.description: The owner's answer to the run's question, relayed by the Tower. Give it to the work once, then acknowledge it; it comes again in every result until acknowledged.

asking.description: The run's last recorded event is a question still waiting on an answer. False with no answer after the runner asked means the answer was lost: ask again.

capability.description: The run's fresh capability token for its org's gateway, replacing the one before, which is revoked: keep only the newest, in memory. Absent when the run has none, is stopping, or its lease is past the four-hour limit.

question.description: With answer: the id of the question it answers, to send back as acked.

stop.description: The Tower asked for the run to stop: stop the work and finish the run as stopped.

worktree_error.description: With worktree_state failed: why the slot could not be prepared.

worktree_state.description: When the run has a slot of the worktree pool: preparing, ready (start the work, if it waits) or failed. Absent when it has none.

methods.name: runner.slot
methods.summary: How a held run's slot of the worktree pool stands: preparing, ready or failed, and why when failed. It reads only: it neither renews the lease nor records anything, so a runner polls it while the slot is prepared and starts the work as soon as it is ready. Refused with fenced unless the runner holds the run under that fence.

params.name: runner
params.description: The runner holding the lease.

params.name: run
params.description: The leased run.

params.name: fence
params.description: The lease's fencing token.

worktree_error.description: With worktree_state failed: why the slot could not be prepared.

worktree_state.description: When the run has a slot of the worktree pool: preparing, ready (start the work, if it waits) or failed. Absent when it has none.

methods.name: runner.finish
methods.summary: Finish a leased run with its outcome.

params.name: runner
params.description: The runner holding the lease.

params.name: run
params.description: The leased run.

params.name: fence
params.description: The lease's fencing token.

params.name: outcome
params.description: done, failed, stopped, lost or needs_owner (the work did not start: its harness needs the owner first).

params.name: pr
params.description: When done: the pull request the work opened.

params.name: reason
params.description: When not done: why. Untrusted.

params.name: need
params.description: When needs_owner, and only then: what the harness needs the owner for: harness_login.

params.name: cost_micros
params.description: The run's cost as its harness reports it, in millionths of a US dollar; absent when unreported. Untrusted.

state.description: The run's final state: done, failed, stopped or lost.

methods.name: runner.permit
methods.summary: Ask the policy engine whether a leased run's Pilot may use a prompted file tool; the decision is recorded before it is returned.

params.name: runner
params.description: The runner holding the lease.

params.name: run
params.description: The leased run.

params.name: fence
params.description: The lease's fencing token.

params.name: tool
params.description: The prompted tool's name, as the harness gave it. Untrusted.

params.name: kind
params.description: read, write, delete, exec or fetch.

params.name: resource
params.description: For a read, write or delete, the absolute path inside the run's directory, empty when the tool names none; for an exec, the shell command; for a fetch, the URL or search. Untrusted text: the engine decides on it as written, and an exec or fetch is recorded redacted, with its SHA-256.

outcome.description: cleared, denied or holding. Only cleared lets the tool run.

methods.name: decisions.list
methods.summary: The decisions that wait on the owner, projected from the event log as the spec's Decision resources (RFC-0035): a Pilot's question, a merge holding for approval, a container operation holding for confirmation. Only the owner's recorded word closes one.

params.name: all
params.description: Every decision the log holds, answered, superseded and archived ones too; only the open ones when false.

answered_by.description: When answered: the actor whose recorded word closed it.

body.description: The Pilot's question, for a question. Untrusted.

id.description: DEC-<seq>: the sequence number of the event that opened it.

options.description: How the owner settles it: each names the owner's command.

description.description: What it does, and the owner's command for it.

proposal_id.description: The id of a supervisor's suggested answer to a question, as questions.list shows it.

proposal_truncated.description: The suggested answer was cut short when recorded: it cannot be accepted; type an answer instead.

proposed.description: Its suggested answer; the owner may accept it with lucy answer <flight> --accept-proposal <id>, the id lucy questions shows.

proposed_by.description: A supervisor that suggested an answer to a question, for example supervisor/rules. A suggestion never closes the decision.

ref.description: The policy decision a merge or container decision is about.

subject.description: The flight, or the container operation.

superseded_by.description: When superseded: the decision that replaced it.

methods.name: config.reload
methods.summary: Load the config directory again and re-run admission, without a restart. A load with no refused resource replaces the config: its statuses are recorded, its Ready Flights dispatched (when the daemon dispatches) and its flights in flight tightened to a stricter posture their config now asks for. A load with refused resources changes nothing but that tightening, which then also moves to owner every flight in flight whose Runway or AutonomyPolicy became invalid or vanished; the last good config stays. A config directory that cannot be read, or no longer exists, fails the reload (failed says why): the last good config stays whole and no flight changes. A loosening never applies to a flight in flight.

applied.description: Whether the new config replaced the old: true when no resource was refused.

failed.description: Why the config directory could not be read, when it could not: the daemon then keeps its last good config whole.

refused.description: The refused resources, each as its source, reason and message, when the reload was not applied.

tightened.description: How many flights in flight moved to a stricter posture.

methods.name: flights.list
methods.summary: Every Flight the daemon loaded, with its goal, its readiness, whether the Tower flies it and the Tower's state of it: lucy's backlog, which lucy flights --json writes as the spec's BacklogTask documents (LUCY-SPEC-017).

flights.description: Every Flight the daemon loaded and admitted, sorted by org and name.

autonomy.description: The posture it is flown under: owner, green or client. For a Flight the Tower flies, the posture its dispatch recorded; otherwise its Runway's, from the AutonomyPolicy level the Runway names, tightened by its own autonomy, or its own. Empty when its posture cannot be set.

cost_micros.description: Its runs' cost as their harness reported it, summed, in millionths of a US dollar. Untrusted.

dispatched.description: Its Dispatched condition: whether the Tower flies it, and why not; empty (no type) when the Flight is not Ready.

last_transition_time.description: When the status last changed, RFC 3339 UTC.

message.description: What a person needs to know.

reason.description: A machine-readable reason, for example SchemaViolation.

goal.description: What the Flight is for, as its config says. Owner-written.

ready.description: Its Ready condition: whether it has what dispatch needs.

last_transition_time.description: When the status last changed, RFC 3339 UTC.

message.description: What a person needs to know.

reason.description: A machine-readable reason, for example SchemaViolation.
Why the flight is in its state, when the Tower says: a grounding reason, for example.

retry_at.description: When the Tower steps the flight again after a failed step, UTC; absent after a clean one.

runs.description: How many runs, one per Pilot generation, the flight has had: its tokens and cost are summed over all of them, so a cost spread over several restarts reads apart from one run's (LUCY-RUN-011).

state.description: The Tower's state of the flight; empty when the Tower does not fly it.

step_error.description: Why the Tower's last step of the flight failed; empty after a clean step.

tokens.description: The tokens its runs' steps reported, summed over every generation (LUCY-RUN-011).

cache_read.description: Input tokens read from the prompt cache.

cache_write.description: Input tokens written to the prompt cache.

methods.name: flights.approve
methods.summary: Approve, as the owner, the merge a flight holds for: the Tower then asks the policy engine again with the approval, bound to the facts it holds now.

params.name: flight
params.description: The flight whose merge holds for the owner.

state.description: The flight's state after the approval.

methods.name: questions.list
methods.summary: The Pilots' open questions, as the Tower records them: each flight that is asking, oldest first.

questions.description: Every flight that is asking, oldest question first; empty when none is.

proposal_id.description: The proposal's id, for example p12; accepting it names it. A newer proposal has a new id.

proposal_truncated.description: The proposed answer was cut short when recorded: it cannot be accepted; type an answer instead.

proposed.description: Its proposed answer, waiting on the owner: the owner answers, with it or not.

proposed_by.description: The supervisor that proposed an answer, for example supervisor/rules; absent when none did.

question.description: The Pilot's question, as the Tower recorded it. Untrusted.

question_sha256.description: The SHA-256, in hex, of question exactly as listed; accepting a proposal names it.

since.description: When the flight started asking, UTC.

methods.name: questions.answer
methods.summary: Answer a flight's open question; the Tower relays the answer to its Pilot and records only its digest.

params.name: flight
params.description: The flight that is asking.

params.name: answer
params.description: The owner's answer. It reaches the Pilot through the Tower; the log keeps only its digest. Required unless accept_proposal is set, and refused with it.

params.name: accept_proposal
params.description: The id of the proposal to answer with, as questions.list shows it: the owner's answer, recorded as the owner's. Refused as stale when the flight's proposal or question changed since.

params.name: question_sha256
params.description: With accept_proposal, required: the question_sha256 questions.list showed, or its first 16 or more hex characters.

state.description: The flight's state after the answer, normally flying.

methods.name: runs.list
methods.summary: Runs and their leases, in the order they were queued.

params.name: after
params.description: Return runs queued after this position; 0 starts at the beginning.

params.name: limit
params.description: At most this many runs; 0 means 100.

more.description: Whether runs after this page existed when it was read.

next.description: Pass as after to read the next page.

runs.description: The runs, in the order they were queued.

activity.description: When the run last did something, UTC.

asking.description: The run's last event was a question.

cost_micros.description: The run's cost as its harness reported it, in millionths of a US dollar. Untrusted.

expires_at.description: When leased: the lease's expiry, UTC.

fence.description: The current or last lease's fencing token.

flight.description: The flight the run is for.

position.description: The run's place in the queue; pass as after to page.

reason.description: When failed, stopped or lost: why. Untrusted.

runner.description: The runner that holds or held it.

state.description: queued, leased, done, failed, stopped or lost.

tokens.description: The tokens the run's steps reported, summed.

cache_read.description: Input tokens read from the prompt cache.

cache_write.description: Input tokens written to the prompt cache.

methods.name: sandbox.held
methods.summary: Operations on an org's container that wait on the owner: each would stop the sessions live in it, oldest first.

held.description: Every container operation that waits on the owner, oldest first; empty when none does.

decision.description: The policy decision that waits; a confirmation names it.

live_sessions.description: The runs live in the container, which the operation would stop.

op.description: up, restart or down: each stops the work running in the container.

org.description: The org whose container it is.

outcome.description: holding, or denied when an earlier confirmation lapsed because the live sessions changed.

methods.name: sandbox.confirm
methods.summary: Confirm stopping the live sessions a waiting container operation names; the daemon's next request for it is then cleared, while those sessions are unchanged.

params.name: org
params.description: The org whose container it is.

params.name: op
params.description: up, restart or down.

params.name: decision
params.description: The waiting decision, as sandbox.held shows it. A newer request replaces it, and a confirmation of the old one is refused.

approval.description: The confirmation's own decision id, which the cleared request will name.

methods.name: gateway.routes
methods.summary: An org's credential gateway routes, as the daemon loaded them from the org's SecretStore binding. No credential is in them.

params.name: org
params.description: The org.

routes.description: Its routes, by name; empty when the org has no gateway binding.

allow.description: What a worker may ask for.

path.description: A clean absolute path prefix that ends at a segment.

credential.description: The credential's name in the org's vault; never its value.

header.description: The header the credential goes in; Authorization when empty.

name.description: What a worker calls it by: the first path element.

prefix.description: Put before the credential in the header.

scope.description: What the credential grants, as policy records it.

methods.name: gateway.use
methods.summary: Decide an org gateway's use of a route's credential through the policy engine, and record the decision and the request, before the gateway forwards it.

params.name: org
params.description: The org.

params.name: route
params.description: The route, which must be in the daemon's config for the org.

params.name: method
params.description: The worker's HTTP method.

params.name: path
params.description: The path the worker sent, in the form the gateway records it: redacted, capped, with the SHA-256 of the whole path.

params.name: upstream
params.description: The host the gateway will call, which must be the route's.

params.name: capability
params.description: The capability token the worker presented. The daemon verifies it first and records only its id; a request without a valid one is refused.

cleared.description: Whether the gateway may forward the request with the credential.

methods.name: gateway.verify
methods.summary: Check the capability token a request to an org's gateway carries, before the gateway reads any credential, and record a refusal as gateway.denied.

params.name: org
params.description: The org.

params.name: route
params.description: The route, which must be in the daemon's config for the org.

params.name: method
params.description: The worker's HTTP method.

params.name: path
params.description: The path the worker sent, in the form the gateway records it: redacted, capped, with the SHA-256 of the whole path.

params.name: upstream
params.description: The host the gateway will call, which must be the route's.

params.name: capability
params.description: The capability token the worker presented. The daemon verifies it first and records only its id; a request without a valid one is refused.

verified.description: Whether the capability is valid for the org, the route and a run still leased under it. False is recorded as gateway.denied; forward nothing.

methods.name: gateway.deny
methods.summary: Record a request an org's gateway refused before any credential was involved.

params.name: org
params.description: The org.

params.name: route
params.description: The route, when the request named a known one.

params.name: method

methods.name: worktree.list
methods.summary: The worktree pool's slots, by org, repository and number: each with its state, the run that holds or last held it, its branch, and why it is held when quarantined or broken.

params.name: org
params.description: Only this org's slots; every org's when empty.

slots.description: The slots, by org, repository and number.

branch.description: The branch the run works on.

head.description: When free or quarantined: the commit it was given back or quarantined with.

number.description: The slot's number in its repository's pool.

prep.description: When leased: how its preparation stands: preparing, ready or failed.

reason.description: Why it is held, when quarantined: uncommitted changes, commits on no remote ref, or its work could not be checked; why it broke, when broken; why its preparation failed, when that failed.

run.description: The run that holds it, or held it last.

state.description: free, leased, quarantined (its run finished with work that has not landed), broken, or discarded.

methods.name: worktree.discard
methods.summary: Discard a quarantined or broken slot of the worktree pool: recorded first, then its directory is removed through the path guard. Its branch stays in the repository's clone, so its commits are recoverable until git gc. Refused unless confirm repeats slot exactly, and for a free or leased slot.

params.name: slot
params.description: The slot, as worktree.list names it: <org>/<repo>/<number>.

params.name: confirm
params.description: The slot again, exactly: the discard removes the slot's directory, and with it any work in it that is not committed.

branch.description: The branch the run works on.

head.description: When free or quarantined: the commit it was given back or quarantined with.

number.description: The slot's number in its repository's pool.

prep.description: When leased: how its preparation stands: preparing, ready or failed.

reason.description: Why it is held, when quarantined: uncommitted changes, commits on no remote ref, or its work could not be checked; why it broke, when broken; why its preparation failed, when that failed.

run.description: The run that holds it, or held it last.

state.description: free, leased, quarantined (its run finished with work that has not landed), broken, or discarded.

methods.name: shadow.import
methods.summary: Record one task of the existing supervisor, as an offline import file holds it (shadow mode, LUCY-RUN-012): its org, class, goal, repository, posture and actions. The daemon checks it against the import format again and refuses a task of an org it has no admitted Airspace for, or one with any value that looks like a credential. The same task again records nothing; a task id imported before with other contents is refused. Nothing is fetched and nothing acts.

params.name: org
params.description: The org, which must have an admitted Airspace.

params.name: task
params.description: The task's id in the import file: lower-case letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'.

params.name: class
params.description: The task's class, which shadow mode compares by and takeover is decided by.

params.name: goal
params.description: The task's goal, in at most 512 bytes. Untrusted.

params.name: repository
params.description: The repository's name.

params.name: posture
params.description: green, owner or client: the posture the task ran under.

params.name: actions
params.description: What the existing supervisor did, in time order, from dispatched.

action.description: dispatched, asked, answered, pr_opened, review_requested, merged, closed or handed_to_owner.

by.description: An answered action's answerer: supervisor or owner. The answer itself is never imported.

checks.description: A pr_opened action's checks: passing, failing or pending.

text.description: An asked action's question, and nothing else's. Untrusted.

outcome.description: recorded, or unchanged when the same task was imported before.

methods.name: shadow.list
methods.summary: The imported tasks of the existing supervisor, by org, class and task.

params.name: org
params.description: Only this org's tasks; every org's when empty.

seq.description: The sequence number of its shadow.task_imported event.

methods.name: runner.host_org
methods.summary: Make org the host org: the one org whose runs runners placed on the host lease, since every process on the host runs as one uid and can reach the others' sockets. The first host lease sets it; only this owner command changes it, recorded, and it is refused with host_org while any host run is live.

params.name: org
params.description: The org whose runs runners placed on the host lease from now on.

runner_org.message: a runner leases for one org

field.description: The params field (or request member) at fault.

help.description: What to change in the request.

request_id.description: Correlation id for an internal error; the daemon's log has the details.
